_comment: #508. The residence parks - St Francis Wood, Forest Hill, Balboa Terrace - are the 1920s-30s
end of the belt rather than the 1900s end: period-revival stucco, whiter and chalkier than Noe,
and much more uniform because they were built as tracts under design review. So the Base draws
sit close together on purpose; the variation the district actually has is small.
The one strong note is Accent2, which ramps stucco tan into terracotta - that is the clay tile
roof and the tile hoods over the openings, the thing that makes these streets identifiably not
Noe Valley. Metal is a paler grey than the belt: these have more steel casements and less
Authored, not verified in an Editor.
